text:
Alex M.: Hey team — quick benefits/payroll questions for my first week. I finished onboarding but not sure when health/dental kick in and I haven't gotten the company pay card yet.
Samira (People Ops): Welcome! :tada: Congrats again. You should get benefits effective the 1st of next month if you enroll within 30 days. Did you complete the online benefits enrollment? <https://hr.redwood.com/benefits-enroll|benefits portal>
Alex M.: I filled the enrollment form during orientation but wasn't 100% sure if it submitted? I clicked Submit but didn't see a confirmation screen.
onboarding-bot: Hi Alex M. — I see an enrollment attempt on 2025-11-28 15:22 UTC (status: pending). Please confirm you uploaded a signed dependent form if adding dependents.
Priya (Benefits): Hi Alex — I can check. If you only enrolled yourself it should be auto-approved. If you added dependents we need the dependent verification docs. Can you DM me which plan you picked (PPO vs HMO)?
Alex M.: Picked PPO. No dependents.
Priya (Benefits): Okay great — status: enrolled, effective date: 2025-12-01. You'll get the benefits welcome packet by email tomorrow with ID card instructions.
Alex M.: Awesome, thanks. About the pay card — I didn't get any physical card or activation email. Do we use direct deposit by default?
Jorge (Payroll): Hey Alex — by default payroll sets up direct deposit if you provided bank details during onboarding. If you didn't, we issue a pay card (issued by Paysa). I don't see direct deposit on your profile. Did you upload a voided check or complete the bank form?
Alex M.: Oops I skipped that step — I thought the recruiter took care of it. What's the bank form link?
Samira (People Ops): Here's the form: <https://hr.redwood.com/payroll/direct-deposit|Direct Deposit Form>. You can also DM me the last 4 of the account and I'll verify. If you prefer the pay card we'll request one — activation link is emailed from paysa@paysacard.com.
Lina (Manager): @Alex M. if it's easier we can get you a pay card for the first cycle and switch to direct deposit after. LMK.
Alex M.: That would be great, thanks Lina. How long until the card arrives?
Jorge (Payroll): If we request a pay card today, standard mail is 5-7 business days. If you need funds sooner we can do same-week ACH to your bank once you submit the direct deposit form (takes 1 payroll cycle to settle).
Alex M.: Ok I'll submit the form tonight. One more quick Q: Do holidays start accruing immediately or is there a waiting period?
Samira (People Ops): Holiday pay follows the company calendar. New hires are eligible immediately for company observed holidays (paid) — no accrual waiting period. PTO accrual starts first full month of employment per policy.
Alex M.: Good to know. For reimbursements (moving expenses) — who should I send receipts to?
Samira (People Ops): For one-off reimbursements, upload receipts to Ramp (expenses@ramp.com) and tag the cost center. For relocation-specific reimbursements we need pre-approval from People Ops — email me the relocation approval and I'll route it.
Alex M.: Perfect. Thanks everyone!
Priya (Benefits): Also note HSA eligibility depends on the plan — PPO you picked is HSA-eligible only with the high-deductible option. If you want HSA setup, reply here and I'll enable it.
Alex M.: Not right now, maybe later.
Jorge (Payroll): Quick note: once you submit the direct deposit form please post a screenshot here and I'll update payroll so you don't get the pay card.
Alex M.: Will do. Thanks :slightly_smiling_face:
Samira (People Ops): Tagging @onboarding-bot to follow up on dependent docs (none) and for a benefits welcome reminder in 24h.
onboarding-bot: Scheduled reminder: benefits-welcome (24h).
Lina (Manager): Welcome aboard again, Alex — shout if you need anything else. :wave:
